channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Missing toll from Nepal, China flood nears 3,000 as race for survivors continues
item.description: Rescuers in Nepal and China on Saturday continued to search for the nearly 3,000 people missing after devastating flooding along the border with China engulfed entire villages earlier this week. At least 682 bodies were recovered in both countries, including 675 in Nepal and seven in China.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Netanyahu condemns 'criminal acts of violence' by settlers in West Bank villages
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday condemned what he called "criminal acts of violence" perpetrated by Israeli settlers in two Palestinian villages. Earlier in August, a group of settlers blocked supplies from entering Palestinian houses on the outskirts of Qusra and attacked a Palestinian family and a foreign media crew in nearby Jalud.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 'I am sure of myself': A look back at Dolly Parton's unspoken feminist legacy
item.description: Beloved country star Dolly Parton was many things to her fans, including an actor, singer, philanthropist and entrepreneur. But after her death on Tuesday at the age of 80, some admirers are remembering her as something she never overtly claimed: feminist icon.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Iran war reaches 6-month mark: Conflict cost $1,100 per US taxpayer
item.description: After six months of war, Iran’s leadership has coalesced around a hard core of military generals and clerics long entrenched in the ruling theocracy. They are ready for a potentially long confrontation with the US and determined to prevent any unrest at home. It’s a far cry from US President Donald Trump’s initial hopes of toppling the Islamic Republic and his subsequent claims that “regime change” had brought more compromising officials to the fore. In an analysis, FRANCE 24's Philip Turle said the war had so far cost around 1,100 US dollars for each US taxpayer.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Extremely risky operations’: Rescuers work amid threat of river banks bursting
item.description: Nearly 3,000 people remained missing on Saturday, while 682 deaths had been confirmed after flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border. Rescue operations remain risky as a lake formed upstream by the floods threatens to burst its banks. FRANCE 24's Shahzaib Wahlah reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Situation in Niger 'not stabilised yet' as security forces deploy around airport
item.description: A group of soldiers in Niger rebelled against officers at a key military base and fired at sensitive locations in the capital, Niamey, in an apparent mutiny marked by gunfire and explosions, authorities said Saturday, in what was seen as a major threat to the country's struggling junta. FRANCE 24's Wassim Nasr brings you this analysis.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Referendum on EU membership: An ‘existential question’ for Icelanders
item.description: As Icelanders head to the polls on Saturday to vote in a referendum on whether the country should resume talks with the EU over membership, FRANCE 24 speaks to Eiríkur Bergmann, Professor of Politics at Bifröst University, for more insight into the vote.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Rescue operations ongoing as death toll continues to rise
item.description: Most arrive with nothing except the clothes they are wearing. As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China entered their fourth day Saturday, authorities continued finding survivors and transporting them to safety. At relief centers, as some arrive, families wait anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Warehouse hit by Russian attack stored munitions, Zelensky says
item.description: A depot that exploded in a Russian strike overnight was owned by the Ukrainian military and stored shells, drones, and other munitions, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Niger's junta says 'regaining control' after clashes in capital
item.description: Niger's ​defense ​ministry said the armed forces were ​progressively ‌retaking ⁠control ‌of sites targeted in ⁠an overnight attack on ​the ‌capital Niamey, according to a ‌statement read ​on state television, which resumed broadcasting ​on ​Saturday after ​temporarily going ​offline.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Several killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza and West Bank
item.description: Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed five people, local hospital officials said Friday. Two brothers and another relative died in a strike on the family’s home outside Khan Younis, officials at Nasser Hospital said. Two separate Israeli strikes killed one person each in Gaza City, according to health officials at Shifa hospital.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepali army uses helicopters to rescue flood survivors
item.description: With roads damaged by the deadly floods, the Nepali army is using helicopters to carry out rescue operations and transport survivors to safety. Meanwhile, skies remain overcast, with more rain expected in the coming hours, raising concerns about further flooding. FRANCE 24's Shahzaib Wahlah reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Dozens dead after Russian drone strike hits warehouse
item.description: At least 27 people have died after a Russian drone struck a depot near Kyiv's western suburbs overnight, sparking a huge fire and explosions, authorities said Saturday. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Mont Blanc ultramarathon trail kicks off amid growing environmental concern
item.description: The annual UTMB, the flagship race of the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc week, kicked off on Friday with 2,500 participants. As the race continues to attract more runners each year, local residents are increasingly concerned about its environmental impact.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Iceland votes on whether to resume EU membership negotiations
item.description: Icelanders go to the polls on Saturday in a referendum on whether to resume membership negotiations with the European Union, in a tight race that will be closely watched in Brussels. The country of just under 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of a 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy. The membership talks were suspended in 2013 when a eurosceptic government came to power.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hundreds evacuate after Russian strike on depot near Kyiv kills at least 37
item.description: A Russian drone strike on a depot on the outskirts of Ukraine's capital Kyiv on Friday killed at least 37 people and forced hundreds to evacuate, Ukrainian authorities said Saturday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: US to control one fifth of Venezuela's oil reserves, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday announced an unprecedented US push ​to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can revive the OPEC nation's battered energy industry while delivering a new source of crude to help bring down US fuel prices.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Russian strikes hit homes, warehouse, shopping mall across Ukraine
item.description: A Russian drone strike triggered a major fire and explosions at a warehouse on the outskirts of Ukraine's capital Kyiv, forcing hundreds to evacuate the region, authorities said early Saturday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal army races to rescue more than 100 trapped in hydropower tunnel after floods
item.description: Nepali army rescue teams were using drilling equipment on Saturday seeking to rescue more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel, three days after devastating floods struck the site.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ligue 1: PSG survive scare to snatch a miraculous 2-2 draw at Lille
item.description: A dramatic start to Matchday 2 in Ligue 1. Just like last week at Rennes, Paris Saint-Germain found themselves 2-0 down, only to produce another miraculous comeback. Vitinha sparked the revival before Marquinhos rescued a point for the Parisians in Lille.
item.dc:creator: L'Equipe TV

item.title: Icelanders vote in tight referendum on restarting EU membership talks
item.description: Iceland will vote Saturday in a tight referendum on whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union. Reykjavik applied for EU membership in 2009, following a financial crisis that devastated its economy, but a eurosceptic government suspended the process in 2013.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Niger junta says it is back in control after soldiers' mutiny rocks capital
item.description: Niger's junta said Saturday it was back in control after mutineers held soldiers hostage at a military base next to the capital's airport. Russian forces reportedly helped members of Niger's presidential guard recapture the air base, killing some of the mutineers, according to diplomatic and security sources.
